messages.content: You write alternative wordings for phrases used in training captions of a map search over US farm country (land cover, distances and NASA POWER climate). Reply with one JSON object only, no other text.

Each key names an OpenStreetMap tag (key=value after 'osm_new.'); there are no wordings yet: write short plain-English noun phrases that name that kind of place.

For every key of the JSON object below, write exactly 12 NEW wordings that mean exactly the same as the existing ones, in plain US English, the way a farmer, planner or analyst might type them. Keep the same grammatical role (a noun phrase stays a noun phrase; a clause that follows a land phrase stays such a clause). Keep every {placeholder} exactly as written, once each, and add no new ones. Keep meanings exact: the same months, the same direction (more or less, within or beyond, highest or lowest). Do not repeat an existing wording. Never use any of these words: airport, church, creek, dam, dike, dirt track, ditch, drainage, dyke, elevator, grain elevator, greenhouse, greenhouses, highway, hospital, landfill, levee, mast, nursery, oil well, orchard, parking, petroleum, power line, power lines, radio, rail, railroad, railway, row of trees, school, shelterbelt, silo, stadium, stream, track, tree row, turbine, vineyard, wind turbine, wind turbines.

Reply with a JSON object with the same keys, each mapped to a list of 12 strings.

{
 "osm_new.power=plant": [],
 "osm_new.leisure=resort": [],
 "osm_new.man_made=clearcut": []
}
